newsitem.title: UK: EBRD says no decision yet on Chernobyl funding.
newsitem.headline: EBRD says no decision yet on Chernobyl funding.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development on Wednesday said it had not yet decided whether to fund new reactors in Ukraine to replace its Chernobyl plant, site of the world's worst nuclear disaster.
But the Bank's president, Jacques de Larosiere, said any decision would be purely on technical grounds.
"There is no political pressure on me...the decision will be on a technical basis only," he told a news conference.
Major industrial nations have asked the EBRD to look into financing two new reactors in Ukraine to replace Chernobyl, which exploded in 1986, sending clouds of radioactive dust across Europe.
There have been media reports that an independent panel of experts had said the project would be uneconomic and that if it was not approved, Kiev was threatening to keep Chernobyl open.
De Larosiere said there were a number of factors to be considered, including cost and safety.
"We are not yet in a position to say whether all those conditions have been met," he said.
